html:
The wars that ended Spanish rule on the American mainland, from 1810 to 1826. They turned Spanish America into the Latin American republics.

The trigger came from Europe. In 1808 Napoleon took the Spanish king prisoner and put his own brother on the throne. In 1810 local councils took power in Caracas, Buenos Aires, Bogotá and Santiago, at first in the captive king's name. In Mexico the priest Miguel Hidalgo called a mass uprising.

The main phases:

  • 1810 to 1815: early revolts; most were crushed once Spain's king returned in 1814, though Buenos Aires held out.
  • 1817 to 1818: San Martín crossed the Andes and freed Chile.
  • 1819 to 1822: Simón Bolívar won Boyacá and Carabobo, freeing what became Colombia, Venezuela and Ecuador.
  • 1821: Mexico became independent under a conservative deal.
  • 1824: the Battle of Ayacucho in Peru broke Spain's last big army; its last mainland fort surrendered in 1826.

Only Cuba and Puerto Rico stayed Spanish, until 1898.
sum: The wars that ended Spanish rule on the American mainland, from 1810 to 1826. They turned Spanish America into the Latin American republics.
